items.body:
## Problem

The Codex desktop app on Windows is noticeably sluggish during ordinary chat use. Local diagnostics show repeated primary-renderer errors:

```text
[desktop-notifications][global-error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
```

The user reports sluggishness; the error counts below are locally verified. No controlled performance trace has established that ResizeObserver is the cause.

## Environment

- Windows x64, Microsoft Store/MSIX installation
- Desktop product version: 26.1007.21434, build 13901, production channel
- Installed package version: 26.1007.2314.0
- Bundled backend reported by the desktop log: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- Observation date: October 10, 2026
- The app's configured update check reported up_to_date during this investigation

## Verified observations

- One current app-run log contains 124 exact ResizeObserver error-line occurrences across approximately 10 minutes. These are log-line counts, not counts of independent user-visible freezes.
- The error records identify the primary renderer. The forwarded records do not identify the observer callback or include a usable component stack.
- Some occurrences are near reasoning-summary updates or failed optional MCP discovery messages. These are temporal associations, not proof of causation.
- A read-only check using the bundled backend's features list reports concurrent_reasoning_summaries as false. No explicit entry was found in the inspected user configuration. This does not establish the effective desktop experiment or per-request override.
- The same log has three guardianv2.thread_context deprecation notices, although the inspected user config contains neither guardianv2 nor thread_context. The exact live source of that override remains unconfirmed.
- A previously observed unknown code_mode_tool_description_first setting is absent from this current run's log and is not claimed to be currently reproduced.

## Reproduction and limits

During ordinary local chat use, the user observes sluggishness and the primary renderer logs the repeated ResizeObserver error above. The exact interaction that triggers each event is not yet isolated. A minimal clean-profile reproduction, source-mapped observer trace, and controlled before/after performance comparison have not been performed.

These observations do not establish a GPU problem, memory leak, database corruption, or a shared cause between the layout error and Guardian warning. No chat deletion, cache reset, or application-bundle patch was performed as part of this report.

## Expected behavior / request

Please investigate the primary-renderer layout/state-update path in this build and provide a supported diagnostic or workaround that preserves chats and settings. Please distinguish genuine performance failures from noisy generic renderer error forwarding and include actionable source/stack diagnostics.

Separately, the Guardian notice should identify the configuration layer supplying the obsolete field rather than directing users to remove a key absent from their local file.

## Related reports

- #39120: Windows typing and mouse stutter with repeated ResizeObserver loops
- #33996: summary-update correlation and later corrections showing multiple possible causes
- #42495: generic renderer error forwarding under a misleading notification prefix
- #50526: deprecated Guardian field despite clean local configuration
- #52747: separate unknown injected session-feature report

## Privacy

Prepared by a Codex assistant at the affected user's explicit request. This report includes only product versions, generic error strings, aggregate counts, and bounded diagnostic conclusions. No raw logs, screenshots, chat content, local usernames or paths, account/session identifiers, credentials, private files, or third-party provider details are attached.

items.body:
Problem
The Windows ChatGPT desktop app imposes a minimum window size larger than the available display work area when Windows accessibility Text size is increased. The composer extends below the display. Windows text size must remain at the user's preferred 147%; forcing all of ChatGPT to 100% is only a workaround.

Versions
MSIX package: OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
Display name / executable: ChatGPT / app/ChatGPT.exe
Internal app version: 26.1007.21434
Electron package dependency: 42.3.0
Executable product version: 155.0.8059.40
Windows build: 10.0.26200, x64

Relevant settings and topology
Windows accessibility TextScaleFactor: 147 (147%). This is separate from monitor display scaling.
Primary: 2560x1440, display DPI 120 (125%), work area 2500x1440.
Wired secondary: 1920x1080, display DPI 144 (150%), work area 1848x1080.
Affected spacedesk secondary: 1366x768, display DPI 96 (100%), work area 1318x768. The taskbar consumes horizontal space, not vertical space.
The user reports the same general symptom on the wired secondary; exact clipping measurements below are from the 1366x768 display.

Reproduction
1. Keep Windows Accessibility > Text size at 147%.
2. Launch ChatGPT normally, without --force-device-scale-factor.
3. Move its main window to the 1366x768 / 100% display.
4. Maximize it and try to access the bottom composer.

Expected
The window fits the display work area and the entire composer remains visible and usable. Windows text size and per-monitor DPI remain respected. Minimum window dimensions should be clamped to the effective work area, with layout adapting when necessary.

Measured actual behavior
All geometry was queried from a per-monitor-DPI-aware diagnostic thread.
Affected display work rectangle: left473, top1440, right1791, bottom2208.
Normal-launch maximized ChatGPT rectangle: left473, top1440, right1791, bottom2322 = 1318x882.
GetDpiForWindow: 96.
WM_GETMINMAXINFO: minTrackSize 706x882.
Bottom extends 114 physical pixels below the work area.
Read-only inspection of the installed main-process bundle found getPrimaryMinimumSize(){return{width:480,height:600}}.
480*1.47=705.6, rounded to706; 600*1.47=882. Both dimensions match the native minimum constraints.
A user-provided screenshot confirmed that the composer was clipped at the display bottom.

Controls / attempts
- Notepad works correctly on the same display (user observation).
- A newly opened ChatGPT main window also reproduces the issue.
- Changing the wired display's scaling from150% to100% did not change the affected window's minTrackSize706x882 or resolve clipping.
- ChatGPT's own F11 fullscreen mode expanded width to1366 but retained height882; clipping remained.
- Starting the same installed executable with --force-device-scale-factor=1 changed minTrackSize to480x600 and the rectangle to1318x768, exactly fitting the work area.
- The user then confirmed that the entire composer was visible and text could be entered.
This controlled workaround strongly links the failure to scaling-dependent minimum-size handling. No reset, app modification, uninstall, or registry write was used.

Regression information
The user reports no such symptom before the update registered on2026-10-10 at15:31 JST.
Previous package26.1002.7124.0 was registered on2026-10-07. We did not run a direct old-version comparison, so the exact introduction point remains unverified.

Separate issue
Windows Repair attempts return0x80073D02 because the package application is in use. This is not treated as the cause of composer clipping, and success of Repair is not the requested outcome.

Requested application fix
Investigate and adapt the fixed480x600 main-window minimum to the current display's effective work area under Windows accessibility text scaling. Ensure minimum-size synchronization happens when the window moves between displays or scale/text-size changes. Preserve147% text scaling and per-monitor DPI; verify restored, maximized, fullscreen, and newly created main windows on1366x768.
Do not treat a force-device-scale-factor shortcut as the permanent fix.

Evidence scope
The precise failing internal component and update commit are not established. Chromium's current official ui/display/win/screen_win.cc multiplies monitor device scaling by UwpTextScaleFactor and bypasses text scaling when a forced device scale factor is supplied. Exact installed Chromium-tag source retrieval was unavailable, so this upstream code is supporting evidence, not proof of an exact commit.
Source: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/master/ui/display/win/screen_win.cc

Privacy
This report deliberately excludes account names, machine names, user filesystem paths, conversation contents, raw logs, and screenshots. This report was prepared with Codex assistance from local read-only diagnostics and user observations, and posted with the user's explicit approval.

items.title: Report exec runtime resets before accepting further requests
items.body:
Report exec runtime resets before accepting further requests

## Why

Replacing a gRPC code-mode runtime loses stored values and running cells. Silently continuing after reconnection hides that loss, while prior external tool operations may already have completed.

## What changed

- Capture the runtime generation when `execute` and `wait` calls are created. If recovery replaces it, reject those calls with an explicit reset error, including concurrent calls and calls first polled after recovery.
- Explain the lost state and advise inspecting prior tool results before retrying. Allow a fresh `exec` call to continue on the replacement runtime.
- Keep `terminate` from reopening the runtime so cleanup cannot hide a reset from the next request.

## Testing

Extend gRPC recovery tests to cover reset errors after host restarts, missing sessions, and route loss, rejection of queued calls, and successful fresh execution with cleared stored state.

3. Move those 12 projects and 7 chats back to the default Projects / Tasks sections. The three custom sections remain present but empty.
4. October 9: the user reports remote access is working again and asks to retry the organization. Recovery was reported after the rollback, but this does not prove rollback alone caused recovery.
5. Reapply the same 12 project moves and 7 chat moves into the same three sections. Local reads of the previously affected task and a shorter control task succeed.
6. October 10: the user reports that the phone cannot connect again after reapplying the sections.

The organization was performed with these Codex app tools:

- `create_sidebar_section`
- `move_project_to_sidebar_section`
- `move_thread_to_sidebar_section`

Local Codex chat moves used `source="codex"`, `hostId="local"`, and the returned custom section ID. One moved chat used `source="chatgpt"`. Projects included local macOS projects, a remote Windows project, and ChatGPT projects. Sidebar grouping was by project, chats sorted by update time. No project membership or execution host was changed as part of the sidebar moves.

### What is the expected behavior?

Moving a project or chat to a custom sidebar section should preserve its original host association and remote ability to load its messages. The phone and another PC should be able to continue opening the same existing local Codex chats after organization.

### Additional information

- This is a repeated temporal association: organize → remote failure; roll back → subsequently reported recovery; organize again → remote failure again. Root cause is not established.
- Local message reads succeeded before and after organization, including another successful read on October 10.
- One affected task has a large local history: approximately 392 MB across two matching rollout files when inspected on October 8, with many image/tool output records. This is a possible confounder, not a confirmed cause or a measurement of the remote request payload. A remote short-task comparison was requested but no result was provided.
- Earlier desktop logs also contained network-change / WebSocket disconnect events, but those have not been correlated to the failing phone request and are not presented as proof.
- Please investigate section serialization, host-qualified chat routing, and remote task-message loading / timeout handling.
- Personal task titles, session identifiers, local paths, account/device identifiers, private conversation contents, and raw logs are omitted from this public report.

items.title: Codex Desktop: no agent-facing native project creation tool, causing workspace setup to stall

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

26.1002.52244, build 13536, bundle ID `com.openai.codex`. Read from the installed application's Info.plist while preparing this report; the About dialog was not independently checked.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon (arm64).

### What issue are you seeing?

I asked Codex to reorganize my existing Codex workspace and create named **native projects**, then place those projects under sidebar sections. I meant the app's project objects, like the existing entries in the Projects page—not ordinary filesystem directories, new chats, or another standalone application.

The assistant could list projects, create sidebar sections, and move existing projects into sections. However, its exposed native app tools had no project-creation operation. It created local directories and described a proposed structure, but no corresponding native projects were registered.

I repeatedly clarified the request and supplied screenshots showing both the project picker and the **… → Projects** management page. The conversation still ended in repeated explanations and requests for me to do the creation manually. This made an otherwise straightforward workspace-organization task take many turns without completing the requested operation.

Observed capability gap in this session:

- Available: `list_projects`, `move_project_to_sidebar_section`, `reorder_sidebar_projects`, and sidebar-section management.
- No `create_project` or equivalent native project-registration tool was exposed.
- Creating a directory did not add a native project.
- Computer Use could not provide a UI route. Calling `cua.getApp("Codex")` returned:

```text
Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.
```

The restriction remained when the session had full filesystem access. Filesystem access and Computer Use policy are separate; this is not evidence that a user permission prompt was missing.

### What steps can reproduce the issue?

This is the observed session sequence, not a reproduction on a clean installation:

1. Open a local Codex Desktop chat with native app tools available.
2. Ask the assistant to create a new named native project and place it in a sidebar section.
3. Clarify that "project" means the app's project object, not a local directory or chat.
4. Inspect the available native tools: project listing and organization are available, but no creation/registration operation is exposed.
5. The assistant can prepare filesystem directories but cannot register them as native projects through those tools.
6. If it attempts the Computer Use route, selecting Codex returns the safety restriction above.
7. Check the project inventory: the requested projects have not been added.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please expose a supported, narrowly scoped native operation to create/register a project with its display name and appropriate local-folder association. It should return a project ID that can be verified with `list_projects` and used by the existing sidebar tools.

The assistant should also distinguish native projects, sidebar sections, local directories, and chats before promising a structure. When creation is unsupported, it should identify that limitation early instead of producing substitute directories, repeatedly asking the user to clarify an already clear request, or suggesting broader permissions will solve it.

The request is for a supported project-management capability. It does not require removing the Computer Use self-targeting restriction.

### Additional information

- In-app feedback was successfully submitted. **Feedback ID: `01a123cb-a16b-7340-99ca-02086b85ba83`**.
- Observed on October 10, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai).
- Related: #23452 documents the Computer Use self-targeting restriction. This report concerns the missing native project-creation operation and its effect on an otherwise supported workspace-organization workflow.
- No new native projects were created during this attempted workflow. Existing projects and the prepared local directories should not be confused with successful creation.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
# Email artifact regression: recipient field left empty despite known recipient

## Summary

ChatGPT generated an email artifact where the intended recipient was known, but the actual recipient field was not populated.

Across three consecutive attempts, the recipient was either omitted, inserted into the email body, or the output was rendered as a document-style artifact rather than a usable email artifact. As a result, the send action was disabled or unavailable.

The same workflow succeeded on the first attempt after switching to GPT-5.5.

This appears to be a structured-output / artifact-schema regression, not a writing-quality issue.

## Expected behavior

When a user asks ChatGPT to draft an email to a known valid recipient:

- the recipient should be mapped to the email artifact’s recipient field;
- the subject should be mapped to the subject field;
- the body should be mapped to the body field;
- the resulting email artifact should be sendable without manual reconstruction.

## Actual behavior

The recipient value was not bound to the structured recipient field. The email UI showed an empty recipient field, so the send action remained disabled or unavailable.

The failure happened across three consecutive attempts:

1. The recipient field was omitted.
2. The recipient was placed inside the body text instead of the recipient field.
3. The output was rendered as a non-email document artifact, so no send action was available.

After switching to GPT-5.5, generating the same email artifact with explicit recipient metadata worked on the first attempt.

## Minimal reproduction pattern

1. Ask ChatGPT to draft an email to a known valid recipient address.
2. Ask for the result as a sendable email artifact.
3. Observe whether the actual recipient field is populated.
4. In the failing case, the recipient is missing, appears only in the body, or the result is rendered as a non-email artifact.
5. The send action remains disabled or unavailable.
6. Repeat the correction attempts.
7. Compare with GPT-5.5 using explicit recipient metadata.

## Impact

This breaks the expected contract between model output and the email artifact UI.

Email drafting depends on strict field binding. If structured fields such as recipient, subject, and body are not reliably mapped, the artifact is functionally unusable even if the generated text is otherwise correct.

The repeated failures also create a trust problem: the assistant may claim that the artifact is fixed while the actual UI remains unusable.

## Related reports checked

I searched for similar reports before filing. The closest related public issues I found concern external sending, recipient verification, approval gates, or broader model reliability, but they do not appear to report this specific email-artifact field-binding failure.

Examples of related but non-duplicate issues:

- #40370: external-contact task hangs at recipient verification.
- #52212: send-time execution gate linking an exact draft to user approval.
- #38742: Gmail write action executed without required confirmation.
- #52158: broader repeated requirement drift and success reporting failures.

## Notes

- Observed in the ChatGPT web UI.
- The issue is not about the email body content.
- The issue concerns structured field binding and artifact schema adherence.
- If this is not the correct public tracker for ChatGPT artifact regressions, please route it to the appropriate internal owner.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

MSIX package: 26.1007.2314.0 

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

### Summary

Appshots fail for certain Windows applications depending on their graphics acceleration settings and window state.

I identified two effective workarounds through controlled testing:

- **Google Chrome:** Appshot capture fails with graphics acceleration enabled, even in windowed mode. Disabling graphics acceleration and restarting Chrome restores capture functionality.
- **WPS Office:** Appshot capture fails in maximized mode but succeeds after restoring the window to a non-maximized state.

Microsoft Edge (windowed) and WeChat can be captured successfully.

### Environment

- ChatGPT Windows desktop app, MSIX package version: `26.1007.2314.0`
- Windows laptop with a single built-in display
- No external monitors
- Tested on October 10, 2026

### Relevant Logs

**Capture source timeout:**

```text
Appshot capture start request finished
hasResponse=true

Windows Appshot completion failed
errorMessage="computer-use request timed out: load_appshot_capture_source"

Appshot capture settled
elapsedMs=2086
failureReason=native_completion_failed
hadAxText=false
hadScreenshot=false
status=failed
```

**Duplicate Appshot requests:**

```text
06:49:05.384Z Appshot hotkey pressed hotkey=DoubleAlt
06:49:05.569Z Appshot hotkey pressed hotkey=DoubleAlt
```

Two capture requests were created for the same Chrome window. One failed with `start_response_missing`, while the other failed with `native_completion_failed`.

A separate attempt successfully captured both the screenshot and accessibility text:

```text
hadAxText=true
hadScreenshot=true
status=success
```

### Analysis

The successful workarounds suggest a possible compatibility issue in the Windows Appshot capture source-loading path involving GPU-accelerated rendering or specific window states.

The observed failures are not limited to the Double Alt shortcut: WPS also timed out when capture was initiated through the Add Context menu.

The duplicate shortcut events may represent a separate issue. Their causal relationship to the capture timeout has not been established.

### Related Issues

- #45234 — `start_response_missing`
- #45353 — `load_appshot_capture_source` timeout

Unlike #45353, this issue occurs on a single-display laptop. The graphics acceleration and window-state workarounds may provide additional diagnostic information.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch ChatGPT for Windows.
2. Open Google Chrome with graphics acceleration enabled.
3. Restore Chrome to windowed mode.
4. Trigger an Appshot using Double Alt or the Add Context menu.
5. Observe the "Unable to attach Appshot" error.
6. Disable graphics acceleration at chrome://settings/system.
7. Restart Chrome and retry.
8. Appshot capture now succeeds.

Additional case:
1. Open WPS Office in maximized mode.
2. Attempt an Appshot; capture fails.
3. Restore WPS to windowed mode.
4. Retry; capture succeeds.

### What is the expected behavior?

Appshots should reliably capture supported application windows regardless of graphics acceleration settings or maximized/windowed state.

A single shortcut activation should initiate one capture request.

### Additional information

Workarounds confirmed:
- Chrome: Disable graphics acceleration.
- WPS Office: Use windowed mode.

Microsoft Edge and WeChat can be captured successfully.

The codex-computer-use-swift.exe helper process is running. Previous logs also contain successful screenshot and accessibility text captures.

Please investigate whether the capture source-loading timeout is affected by GPU rendering or window presentation state.

items.title: Codex "Selected model is at capacity" / server_overloaded on trivial first turn (Web + Windows app)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
SUMMARY

Codex tasks start normally but fail after ~49 seconds with:

Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.

Internal classification reported by OpenAI Help Center: codex_error_info: server_overloaded

The failure occurs on a trivial first turn. In the primary reproduction the user's entire
prompt was a single short greeting. No tools were invoked, no files were touched, no
tool-call round-trips occurred. The request was rejected while still in its first
inference round. This rules out long-context, large-payload, tool-loop, and client-side
resource causes.

The failure is NOT account-level quota exhaustion. Local response headers captured at the
time of failure show the account had 93 percent of its window remaining:

x-codex-plan-type = pro
x-codex-primary-used-percent = 7
x-codex-credits-has-credits = True
x-codex-credits-balance = 62500
x-codex-primary-window-minutes = 10080 (7-day window, ~432000s until reset)

This report includes full client-side telemetry because the backend routing logs are not
reachable from the client.

REPRODUCTION

Surface Codex Web (chatgpt.com/codex/) + ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop app
App version 26.1007.21434
CLI version codex-cli 0.155.1 (npm global)
OS Windows 10, build 19045
Prompt that triggered it single short message (two characters)
Network Normal network AND mobile hotspot (rules out local network path)
Control Regular ChatGPT web chats work normally during the same period
Models affected gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-6-luna -- all three
Reasoning efforts ultra, xhigh, high, medium, low
Transport Both responses_http and responses_websocket

TIMELINE (Asia/Hong_Kong, UTC+8)

All timestamps extracted from the local SQLite log database shipped with the app at
~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite, table "logs", column "feedback_log_body", which records the full
request span for every turn.

11:47:55 thread 01a123ec-aaf8-7d73-a720-5a216a3abd6b created
11:53:48 thread 01a123f2-0d5b-7c63-b551-4789bec089d5 created (fork of 01a123ec)
11:55:09 gpt-5.6-sol -> at capacity
11:56:02 gpt-5.6-sol -> at capacity
11:56:34 gpt-5.6-sol -> at capacity (thread 01a123f2)
11:56:35 gpt-5.6-sol -> at capacity (thread 01a123ec, same second)

The reported failure time (11:56:35) is confirmed in local logs.

ERROR RATE TREND (gpt-6-astra)

Capacity errors are monotonically worsening, not a transient spike:

2026-10-04 5,776 requests 8 errors 0.1 percent
2026-10-08 849 requests 10 errors 1.2 percent
2026-10-10 279 requests 13 errors 4.5 percent

A 45x degradation over 6 days with no change in client configuration.

CAPACITY ERRORS BY MODEL

gpt-6-astra 31
gpt-5.6-sol 12
gpt-6-luna 6

Three independent model pools failing simultaneously indicates a shared upstream capacity
constraint, not a single-model issue.

ARTIFACTS

Primary session (the one that failed):

Thread ID: 01a123f2-0d5b-7c63-b551-4789bec089d5
Created: 2026-10-10 11:53:48 Asia/Hong_Kong
Root session: 01a123ec-aaf8-7d73-a720-5a216a3abd6b
Shared link: https://chatgpt.com/s/cx_6ac9d8c818508191bf3ff7999a31e695

Note on identifiers: OpenAI Help Center provided 01a1247e-1d32-7a41-ab4e-6da6ae6e09b7 as
the Session ID for this incident. Local logs show that thread was created at 14:26:47,
2.5 hours AFTER the 11:56:35 failure, so it could not have produced the error. The field
above is the verified thread.

EXPECTED

Task continues or completes normally. Capacity-based failures should either be
transparent (automatic fallback / queueing) or degrade gracefully rather than surfacing a
hard error after the task has already started and consumed work.

ACTUAL

Hard failure with "at capacity" / server_overloaded after the task has been running for
~49 seconds. The session cannot be resumed past the failure point in that turn.

ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS

Client-side model selection diverges from config.toml. The Windows app persists its own
model choice in ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json
(electron-persisted-atom-state.composer-recent-model-configurations-v1) and this takes
precedence over config.toml. Users who edit config.toml to change models may silently
keep running the app-selected model. This may cause confusion when reproducing.

service_tier has no observable effect on capacity errors. priority / "Fast" is
available on all affected models for this account (default_service_tier: null), yet
capacity errors occur regardless. If priority is not expected to guarantee capacity,
that is fine, but it would help to document what it does guarantee.

Harmless but noisy warning on every new thread/fork:
WARN codex_features: unknown feature key in config: code_mode_tool_description_first
The Windows app emits a config key the CLI does not recognize. It is emitted on every
fork / thread spawn and floods the log.

Intermittent model-list timeout:
ERROR codex_models_manager: list_models{refresh_strategy=online}:
failed to refresh available models: request timed out
This can cause the model picker to fall back to a stale cached list, which may hide
newly available models during an incident.

HOW TO REPRODUCE FROM LOGS

For anyone triaging client-side, this is the query that produced the timeline above
(requires the SQLite DB shipped with the app at ~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite):

SELECT datetime(ts,'unixepoch','+8 hours') AS local_time,
level,
target,
feedback_log_body
FROM logs
WHERE feedback_log_body LIKE '%at capacity%'
ORDER BY id DESC;

Identifying which thread actually failed requires the thread_id= span field, not the
session_id field. Forked child threads inherit the parent's session_id in session_meta, so
session_id alone is ambiguous across forks.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434 VSCode-Codex – OpenAI’s coding agent

### What subscription do you have?

26.1007.21434 VSCode-Codex – OpenAI’s coding agent

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Severity: Critical — User-Defined Permission Boundaries Are Not Being Enforced

### Summary

I am reporting a serious and unacceptable issue with the VS Code Codex extension.

**Codex modified files, executed Python commands, and generated additional output files without requesting or receiving my approval, despite my explicit sandbox and approval configuration.**

This is not a minor UI inconvenience or a misunderstanding of how the approval mechanism works. This is a direct inconsistency between the security restrictions I explicitly configured and the permissions actually granted to the agent.

I expect an AI coding agent to respect the permission boundaries established by its user. In this case, those boundaries were not enforced as configured.

### 1. Explicit Security Configuration

My Codex configuration file is located at:

`C:\Users\Administrator\.codex\config.toml`

It explicitly contains:

```toml
approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "read-only"
```

These settings are intentional.

I specifically configured Codex to operate in a restricted environment because I do not want an AI agent independently modifying project files or executing potentially consequential commands without my authorization.

**I did not authorize Codex to operate with workspace-write permissions.**

### 2. Actual Unauthorized Behavior

During a session on October 10, 2026, I asked Codex to write a Python script for visualizing experimental results.

Without requesting my approval, Codex performed the following actions:

1. Executed a PowerShell command to inspect CSV files.
2. Created a new Python script, `plot_frame_subsampling.py`, containing approximately 187 lines of code.
3. Executed the Python compiler using `python -m py_compile`.
4. Executed the newly created Python script.
5. Generated an additional PNG output file in my project directory.

The recorded commands included:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem chouzhen -Filter '*.csv' |
Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
```

```powershell
& 'D:\ProgramData\AnacondaEnvs\test_asr\python.exe' -m py_compile script/plot_frame_subsampling.py
```

```powershell
& 'D:\ProgramData\AnacondaEnvs\test_asr\python.exe' script/plot_frame_subsampling.py --output tmp/frame_subsampling_accuracy.png
```

**At no point did Codex present an approval request before performing these operations.**

I did not explicitly authorize execution of the generated script.

The fact that Codex considered these operations useful for validating its work does not justify bypassing my configured restrictions.

### 3. Evidence: Actual Session Permissions Contradict My Configuration

I inspected the Codex session logs and extracted the effective approval and sandbox settings from the `turn_context` records.

The relevant entry is:

```text
TimeUTC                  Approval     Sandbox
2026-10-10T05:07:04.422Z on-request   workspace-write
```

This is the central issue.

My explicitly configured sandbox mode was:

```toml
sandbox_mode = "read-only"
```

However, the session actually ran with:

```text
sandbox_policy.type = workspace-write
```

**Codex was operating with a higher level of file-system permission than I explicitly configured.**

This is not speculation. The discrepancy is directly observable in the session logs.

I also checked the relevant project-level configuration locations and found no additional `sandbox_mode` setting overriding my user-level configuration.

### 4. VS Code Extension Does Not Provide an Explicit Read-Only Option

The VS Code Codex extension currently presents me with only three permission options:

- Ask for Approval
- Automatic Approval / Let Codex Handle Approvals
- Full Access

There is no visible option to select an explicitly read-only sandbox or to force the extension to use my existing `config.toml` restrictions.

The "Ask for Approval" option was selected when the behavior occurred.

Yet the agent was still allowed to modify files and execute Python commands without requesting my permission.

This raises a critical question:

**Why is a VS Code permission preset apparently taking precedence over an explicitly configured read-only sandbox, without clearly informing the user?**

If the extension overrides security-related configuration, that behavior must be transparent, predictable, and properly documented.

A UI label suggesting that approval is required must not give users a misleading sense of control.

### 5. Why This Is a Serious Security and Trust Issue

I use Codex in a research and software development environment where files, experiment results, and execution environments must be handled carefully.

Unauthorized operations can potentially:

- Modify important source code or experimental configurations.
- Generate, overwrite, or delete research artifacts.
- Execute scripts with unintended side effects.
- Consume computational resources without permission.
- Undermine the reproducibility and integrity of experiments.

I am not claiming that all these consequences occurred in this particular incident. However, the observed behavior demonstrates why the permission boundary matters.

**A coding agent must not silently grant itself more operational freedom than the user explicitly configured.**

This is especially concerning because users may reasonably rely on `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` as a meaningful restriction.

### 6. Expected Behavior

When a user explicitly configures:

```toml
approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "read-only"
```

I expect the following:

1. The VS Code extension should honor the configured sandbox restrictions unless an explicit, clearly disclosed override has been selected.
2. The agent should not silently switch to `workspace-write`.
3. File modifications should require authorization when prohibited by the active sandbox.
4. Commands requiring elevated sandbox permissions should not execute without approval.
5. The effective permission mode should be clearly visible and verifiable.
6. Any conflicting configuration should produce a clear warning instead of silently weakening the user's intended restrictions.

### 7. Actual Behavior

Instead:

- My configuration specified `read-only`.
- The session log reported `workspace-write`.
- Codex created a Python file.
- Codex executed Python commands.
- Codex generated an output image.
- No approval request was presented.

These are concrete, reproducible observations from my environment.

### 8. Requested Action From the Codex Team

I am requesting that the maintainers treat this as a high-priority permission enforcement issue rather than a routine feature request.

Specifically, I request:

1. **Investigate why the VS Code extension did not honor my explicit `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` configuration.**
2. Identify which component or configuration layer changed the effective sandbox mode to `workspace-write`.
3. Fix any unintended or undocumented permission override behavior.
4. Provide an explicit, reliable read-only permission mode in the VS Code extension.
5. Ensure that users can inspect the effective approval and sandbox settings before an agent performs operations.
6. Clarify which operations may execute without approval and which require explicit authorization.
7. Consider adding a strict manual-approval mode for users who need every command execution and file modification to require approval.

### 9. Final Statement

I need to emphasize that **this is not simply about an agent being overly proactive**.

It is about whether explicitly configured security restrictions are actually respected.

If I configure an agent to operate in a read-only sandbox, I should be able to trust that it will not silently operate with write permissions.

If a VS Code extension can override these restrictions without sufficiently clear disclosure, then the permission model is not providing the level of control users reasonably expect.

**I consider this behavior unacceptable for a development tool with direct access to local source code and execution environments.**

I expect a technical explanation of why the effective permissions differed from my configuration, and a concrete fix or supported workaround.

Please investigate this issue seriously.

---

**Environment**

- Product: OpenAI Codex VS Code Extension
- OS: Windows
- Approval policy configured: `on-request`
- Sandbox mode configured: `read-only`
- Effective approval policy: `on-request`
- Effective sandbox mode: `workspace-write`
- Date observed: October 10, 2026
- Extension version: [To be filled in]
- VS Code version: [To be filled in]

**Evidence available:** VS Code screenshots, `config.toml`, command execution history, and Codex session log showing the effective sandbox permissions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and open the OpenAI Codex extension in VS Code on Windows.

2. Open the Codex configuration file at `C:\Users\Administrator\.codex\config.toml` and explicitly configure:

   ```toml
   approval_policy = "on-request"
   sandbox_mode = "read-only"
   ```

3. Save the configuration and restart VS Code.

4. Open a local Python project using the Codex extension.

5. In the Codex interface, select **"Ask for Approval"** (请求批准), which is the most restrictive option available in my extension's permission menu. There is no visible "Read-only" or "Custom Configuration" option.

6. Start a new Codex conversation and ask it to create a Python script for plotting experimental results from existing CSV files. Do not explicitly authorize it to execute any Python code.

7. Observe that Codex proceeds to perform the following operations **without displaying any approval request**:

   - Reads project files using PowerShell commands.
   - Creates a new Python script (`plot_frame_subsampling.py`).
   - Executes Python compilation using `python -m py_compile`.
   - Executes the generated Python script.
   - Generates an additional PNG output file.

8. Inspect the Codex session log under `C:\Users\Administrator\.codex\sessions\` and examine the `turn_context` entry.

   The recorded effective permissions were:

   ```text
   Approval: on-request
   Sandbox:  workspace-write
   ```

   Despite the explicit configuration:

   ```toml
   sandbox_mode = "read-only"
   ```

### Expected Behavior

Codex should honor the explicitly configured `read-only` sandbox, and should not modify project files or run commands requiring elevated sandbox permissions without explicit user approval.

### Actual Behavior

Codex silently operated with `workspace-write` permissions instead of the configured `read-only` mode. It created files and executed Python commands without presenting an approval request.

**The effective sandbox permissions directly contradicted the user's explicit configuration.**

### Additional Notes

This behavior was observed in the VS Code Codex extension on Windows on October 10, 2026.

The exact mechanism causing the permission override has not yet been determined. However, the discrepancy is confirmed by the `turn_context` session log.

The steps above describe the environment and sequence in which the issue occurred; repeatability across fresh sessions has not yet been verified.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Codex VS Code extension must strictly respect the user's explicitly configured security and approval settings.

When the configuration specifies:

```toml
approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "read-only"
```

**The expected behavior is:**

1. **Strict enforcement of the configured sandbox:** Codex must operate in `read-only` mode, not silently override it with `workspace-write` or any less restrictive permission level.

2. **Explicit approval before restricted operations:** Any file creation, modification, deletion, or command execution that requires permissions beyond the read-only sandbox must require explicit user approval before proceeding.

3. **No silent permission escalation:** The VS Code extension must never silently grant broader permissions than those explicitly configured by the user. If a permission preset conflicts with the configuration, the extension must clearly inform the user and require explicit confirmation.

4. **Reliable manual control:** Users must be able to prevent unauthorized file modifications and command execution. Approval requests should remain pending until the user explicitly approves or rejects them, rather than automatically authorizing operations after a timeout.

5. **Consistent and transparent permissions:** The effective sandbox permissions recorded in session logs must match the user's selected and configured restrictions, unless an override has been explicitly authorized and clearly communicated.

**Under no circumstances should Codex silently switch from `read-only` to `workspace-write` and subsequently modify project files or execute commands requiring elevated permissions without user approval.**

This is a fundamental requirement for the reliability, predictability, and trustworthiness of an AI coding agent operating on a user's local development environment.

**User-defined security boundaries must be enforced, not treated as optional preferences.**

items.title: CLI: /restart into the updated executable and resume the current session

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI / TUI, installed through npm, running in Warp on macOS (Apple Silicon, zsh). Installed package checked for this report: `@openai/codex` **0.162.1**.

### What feature would you like to see?

Add a native `/restart` command that cleanly exits the current CLI runtime, launches the **currently installed executable**, and automatically resumes the **same conversation** in the **same terminal pane**.

#### Use case and current workflow

I keep Codex sessions open in Warp while upgrading the npm package. Updating the package on disk does not switch an already-running session to the new executable. I then have to exit each session, launch Codex again from the correct directory, and resume the matching conversation.

The desired sequence is:

1. Update the installed Codex package using the existing update mechanism, for example from another terminal.
2. In an existing Codex session, run `/restart`.
3. Complete the normal shutdown/cleanup sequence, then launch the updated CLI with the equivalent of `codex resume <current-session-id>`.
4. Continue the same conversation in the existing Warp pane.

A per-session command is sufficient. The first implementation does not need to update packages itself or broadcast restarts to other terminals.

#### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- **Load the installed version:** after upgrading from version A to B, restarting an A session must run B. Re-entering a TUI loop inside the old executable would not satisfy this requirement.
- **Resume the exact conversation:** retain its session/thread ID and persisted history, without opening a picker, creating a new conversation, or selecting another session via `--last`.
- **Preserve the terminal and launch context:** keep the same terminal pane and working directory; carry relevant launch/profile overrides through normal resume behavior. Do not replay the original prompt or image attachments.
- **Exit cleanly:** use the normal `/exit` shutdown path, including its handling of an active turn, and allow session persistence and terminal cleanup to finish before relaunching.
- **Remain a native CLI operation:** no tmux migration, external PTY supervisor, or shell wrapper should be required. Other open terminals and unrelated sessions should remain usable.
- **Handle relaunch failure clearly:** report an actionable error and the exact manual resume command. Avoid repeatedly relaunching or rerunning an update command.

### Additional information

#### Source observations

In the inspected [0.162.1 CLI exit/update implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs#L757), `handle_app_exit` prints exit information and optionally runs the update action. A successful package update prints “Update ran successfully! Please restart Codex.” and returns.

This suggests keeping the change around the existing exit/resume lifecycle. The important requirement is an executable handoff after cleanup, resolving the updated installation entrypoint rather than retaining a replaced or version-specific old binary path. The implementation choice is left to maintainers.

Restarting only the shared app-server daemon is a different operation: this request concerns the foreground CLI executable and its current conversation. Shared-daemon handling should follow normal startup compatibility behavior without forcibly interrupting unrelated sessions.

#### Related discussions and overlap

- **#37628 — Add /restart to reinitialize Codex and resume the current thread:** substantial overlap. This issue adds the package-upgrade use case and an explicit requirement to load the new executable. It is not intended to suggest that the earlier request has already been accepted or rejected. Please consolidate into #37628 if that is the preferred tracking issue.
- **#48831 — Automatically relaunch after accepting the startup update prompt:** related executable-handoff work, but scoped to startup before entering the intended interactive session. This request starts from an already-running conversation and must preserve its identity.
- **#9240 — Restart Codex after completing update flow:** a previous, unmerged implementation attempt. Its [Windows launcher review](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/9240#discussion_r2695773410) is relevant when considering npm `.cmd`/`.bat` entrypoints.

#### Suggested validation

Exercise an A-to-B package upgrade followed by restart/resume; verify the running version, exact session ID, history, working directory, and terminal usability. Also cover relevant launch overrides, startup-prompt non-replay, clean shutdown, and an unavailable relaunch target. A Unix executable handoff and Windows npm launcher behavior should both be considered for a cross-platform implementation.

The installed package version and cited source were inspected. No real upgrade/restart experiment or local build/test was performed for this report; the above are proposed acceptance checks.

This is a feature/design request under the current contribution policy. @etraut-openai, could you help assess whether this fits the CLI lifecycle direction or route it to the appropriate maintainer?

### What issue are you seeing?

When using a custom model with a custom API key environment variable, Codex is unable to read that environment variable specified in a terminal.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a custom model to use, through `config.toml`:

   ```toml
   model = "qwen3.8-27b"
   model_provider = "qwen3_8_27b"

   [model_providers.qwen3_8_27b]
   name = "Qwen3.8-27B"
   base_url = "https://<ip>:<port>/v1" # redacted
   env_key = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
   http_headers = { key = "value" } # redacted
   ```

2. Start codex using:

   ```bash
   export OPENAI_API_KEY=xxxxxxxx
   codex
   ```

3. Randomly ask a question. It produces the error:

   > Missing environment variable: \`OPENAI_API_KEY\`.

### What is the expected behavior?

It should use the environment variable for the API key and output responses normally.

### Additional information

A workaround to make it work: Start codex with

```
codex -c 'model="qwen3.8-27b"'
```

Where the `model` field corresponds with the one specified in `config.toml`.

<USERPROFILE>\.cache\codex-runtimes\codex-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe -u <USERPROFILE>\.codex\plugins\cache\openai-curated-remote\chatgpt-meetings\0.8.77\scripts\meetings_mcp_entrypoint.py --profile production

items.title: Desktop app UI switched to English after update - MSIX manifest declares only en-US while zh-CN localization is bundled

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using

`26.1002.7124.0` (updated from `26.930.7945.0` on 2026-10-10)

Also staged with the same problem: `26.1007.2314.0`

Windows deployment event log confirms the update:

```
2026-10-10 13:53:39  OpenAI.Codex_26.930.7945.0 is updating to OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0
2026-10-10 13:54:20  new preferred version: OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0
```

## What issue are you seeing

After the automatic update the Codex App UI switched from Simplified Chinese to English. The Windows display language is `zh-CN` and was not changed.

| | Version | UI |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 26.930.7945.0 | Chinese (correct) |
| After | 26.1002.7124.0 | English (broken) |

The app still ships full Simplified Chinese localization, but it is never loaded:

- `app\locales\zh-CN.pak` exists (508.6 KB)
- `app.asar` -> `.vite/build/locales/zh-CN.json` contains the translations, e.g. `"??"`, `"??"`, `"??"`

Root cause appears to be the MSIX manifest, which declares **only English**:

```xml
<Resources>
    <Resource Language="en-US" />
</Resources>
```

Because of that, Windows reports the app language as `en-US`, so the app resolves its UI locale to English and skips the bundled Chinese resources.

The i18n bundle also hardcodes the fallback locale: `yK = "en-US"` and when the resolved locale is `en-US` an empty message set is used.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows with display language `zh-CN` (`Get-WinUILanguageOverride` = `zh-Hans-CN`)
2. Install / update the Codex App to `26.1002.7124.0`
3. Launch the app
4. The whole UI renders in English

Evidence that Windows still reports Chinese to the app:

- The app's own embedded browser profile shows `intl.selected_languages = "zh-CN,zh"`
- Sentry scope records `culture.locale = "zh-CN"`

## Expected behavior

The UI should be in Simplified Chinese, or at least follow the OS display language, because `zh-CN` localization is bundled with the app.

## Additional information

Verified the installed package contents directly (with admin rights):

- `AppxManifest.xml` declares only `<Resource Language="en-US" />` ? identical in both `26.1002.7124.0` and `26.1007.2314.0`
- `app\locales\zh-CN.pak` is present
- `app.asar` contains `.vite/build/locales/zh-CN.json` with the Chinese strings

There is **no user-facing language setting** anywhere in the app to work around this. Checked:

- `~/.codex/config.toml` ? no `language` / `locale` key
- `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json` ? no language key
- `%APPDATA%\Codex\**` (incl. Local Storage / IndexedDB / Preferences) ? no app-level language setting
- The zh-CN translation catalog contains no "language" setting entry

Also tested: launching the already-running instance via `IApplicationActivationManager` with `--lang=zh-CN` respawns renderer processes with `--lang=zh-CN`, but the UI stays English (the main-process locale is fixed at startup).

**Request:** add the supported languages to the MSIX manifest (e.g. `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ja-JP` ...), or expose a user-facing language setting.

Affected users: every non-English Windows user, with no in-app workaround.

Observed process: - Executable: codex.exe - PID: 33916 - Started: approximately 13:22 via Windows Terminal - Private Bytes: increased from 6.74 GB to 7.23 GB - Working Set: approximately 5 GB - Growth: approximately 128 MB over 20 seconds (~6.4 MB/s) - CPU usage: consistently low Process Explorer confirms that the memory belongs directly to codex.exe (PID 33916), not to child processes. The growth was observed while the process was running, without a corresponding increase in CPU activity. The specific allocation source has not yet been identified. This is suspected to be a CLI-side memory leak or excessive memory retention, rather than an issue in a spawned subprocess. A heap or allocation profile would be needed to confirm the root cause. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Launch Codex CLI 0.162.1 from Windows Terminal on Windows 11. 2. Keep a Codex CLI session running and perform normal interactive usage. 3. Open Sysinternals Process Explorer. 4. Locate the running codex.exe process and monitor its Private Bytes and Working Set. 5. Observe that Private Bytes can grow to more than 7 GB and continue increasing even while CPU usage remains low. Observed instance: PID 33916, started at approximately 13:22. This has been observed in an existing session, but a deterministic minimal reproduction is not yet available. The exact workload or feature responsible for the allocations is unknown. ### What is the expected behavior? Codex CLI should maintain reasonably bounded memory usage during normal interactive sessions. Memory associated with completed tasks, temporary buffers, tool results, or conversation processing should be released or reused when no longer needed. The CLI process should not continuously accumulate multiple gigabytes of private memory without a corresponding active workload. ### Additional information Process Explorer measurements: - Private Bytes: 7,625,948 K (~7.27 GiB) - Working Set: 5,288,844 K (~5.04 GiB) - CPU: ~0.13% - PID: 33916 Executable path: D:\Work\nodejs\node_global\node_modules\@openai\codex\node_modules\@openai\codex-win32-x64\vendor\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex.exe The process was confirmed to be a native codex.exe executable, not node.exe, and no direct child process was identified as responsible for its memory usage. Other Codex instances have substantially lower memory usage, suggesting this behavior may be session-specific rather than a constant baseline overhead. Screenshots from Process Explorer and the initial investigation are available. No heap dump or allocation trace has been collected yet. The root cause is not confirmed. A workaround is to exit and restart the affected CLI process, which releases its allocated memory.

items.title: [macOS] managed-worktree-archive-queue hot retry loop (~45-68 retries/s) pegs main process CPU; survives app restarts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex App 26.1007.21159 (build 20052), bundle id `com.openai.codex`, executable `ChatGPT`

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm` (macOS 26, Apple Silicon)

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop app's main process pegged one core (87% CPU, 72 threads) even while idle. The main-process log (`~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/...`) showed a hot retry loop with no backoff, ~45–68 entries per second, all identical:

```text
info [managed-worktree-archive-queue] Worktree archive will be retried errorMessage="Could not confirm the task's archive status." errorName=Error errorStack="Error: Could not confirm the task's archive status.\n    at #f (.../app.asar/.vite/build/main-*.js:1047:40438)\n    at async #u (...:1047:38907)\n    at async #y (...:1047:22187)" phase=queued
```

Measured: 4,072 such lines in a 60-second window. Fully quitting (Cmd+Q) and relaunching the app did **not** help — the loop resumed within ~2 seconds of startup in the fresh log, so the queue entry is persisted or re-derived at launch.

The trigger appears to be stale managed-worktree directories under `~/.codex/worktrees/` whose `.codex-worktree-name` marker file is **empty (0 bytes)**. I had two such directories (`077f`, created Oct 8; `sync-community-v3-17-0`, created Sep 28). These were likely orphaned by cloud tasks around the time I switched from a custom `model_provider` in `config.toml` back to a regular ChatGPT account, so the app can no longer confirm the corresponding task's archive status. Moving both directories out of `~/.codex/worktrees/` stopped the loop immediately (no restart needed) and CPU dropped from ~87% to 0.2%.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a directory under `~/.codex/worktrees/` (e.g. `~/.codex/worktrees/stale-entry/`) containing only an empty marker file: `touch ~/.codex/worktrees/stale-entry/.codex-worktree-name`
2. Launch / keep running the Codex desktop app
3. Observe the main-process log fill with `[managed-worktree-archive-queue] Worktree archive will be retried ... Could not confirm the task's archive status.` dozens of times per second, and sustained high CPU on the `ChatGPT` main process

(Repro steps inferred from the state on my machine; I have not re-introduced the entry to double-check, but removing the two stale directories is what stopped the loop.)

### What is the expected behavior?

- The worktree archive queue should retry with backoff and eventually give up or surface an actionable error, instead of retrying every ~25 ms indefinitely
- A malformed/orphaned managed-worktree entry (empty `.codex-worktree-name`, task no longer resolvable) should not cause an unbounded hot loop, and should not survive app restarts

### Additional information

- Log location: `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/2026/10/10/codex-desktop-*.log`
- Possibly related theme (hot recovery loops in the desktop app) but a different mechanism: #51087 covers an archived-thread `thread/resume` loop; this one is the managed-worktree **archive** queue
- Workaround for anyone hitting this: quit the app, move stale directories out of `~/.codex/worktrees/` (check for empty `.codex-worktree-name` files), relaunch

items.title: Meetings (Beta) exceeds four-hour limit and remains stuck after HTTP 413 finalization failures

labels.name: bug

labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT/Codex macOS 26.1007.21159 (build 20052), verified from the installed application bundle at diagnosis. Meetings (Beta) plugin 0.8.77; running native Meetings companion 0.5.0 (build 27). The app's update check reported up to date at diagnosis.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro ($200 plan).

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple Silicon.

Output of `uname -mprs`:

```text
Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm
```

### What issue are you seeing?

I recorded a meeting beyond four hours without an automatic stop. After I stopped it, Meetings remained on “Taking notes” for hours. Capture had stopped locally, but upload finalization repeatedly returned HTTP 413. The server continued reporting the meeting as recording, without a recording end time.

The relevant recorded failure fields are:

```text
capture_phase=stopped
delivery_phase=finalizing
recovery_failure=v1:t:finalize:http:413:0
failure_category=http-rejected
http_status=413
recovery_outcome=retry-scheduled
stream_end_called_at=null
```

After preserving the audio and backing up the recovered notes Page, I tried the installed plugin's existing note reprocessing operation once. It returned HTTP 409 Conflict, without a workflow acknowledgement. The plugin client reported:

```text
Meetings returned an invalid reprocessing response.
```

The recording and processing state did not change after that request.

A second guarded attempt at 09:01 UTC captured the server's actual HTTP 409 response:

```text
Recording end could not be confirmed. Stop the recording before reprocessing.
```

Local capture was already stopped, with no active capture lease. The native companion reported idle with Stop disabled. Its existing targeted upload retry operation returned `native companion operation is unsupported`; the upload queue read exposed no items. Reprocessing is therefore blocked on a recording end that local finalization has not successfully confirmed to the server. The client replaces this specific server explanation with the generic error above.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed in one session on October 9–10, 2026:

1. Start taking notes with Meetings (Beta) in the macOS desktop app.
2. Continue beyond four hours. My session included pause/resume after the four-hour point; it had already exceeded four hours before the first pause.
3. Stop after approximately 4 hours 57 minutes of captured audio (5 hours 12 minutes elapsed, including pauses).
4. Observe “Taking notes” persisting for hours while upload finalization automatically retries and receives HTTP 413.
5. Request reprocessing for that existing note after preserving the recording. In this case, the request returned HTTP 409 and did not resolve the state.

This is a native Meetings recording workflow, so a code snippet, Codex token usage, and context-window usage are not applicable. I have not reproduced it in a second long recording. Private recording/session identifiers are omitted from this public report.

### What is the expected behavior?

The [Meetings documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001546-the-meetings-plugin-in-chatgpt) says sessions stop automatically at four hours.

After stopping, the recording should either finish uploading and processing or display the actual failed stage with a usable recovery path. A retry should provide an actionable result while protecting captured audio and existing notes.

### Additional information

- At 06:58:23 UTC on October 10, there had been 76 logged HTTP 413 finalization failures. Reported acknowledgement lag remained unchanged across checked retries; those retry attempts logged zero accepted frames. This does not mean earlier uploads accepted no frames.
- At initial diagnosis, the preliminary transcript stopped around 4:43:11 and the notes Page contained only an empty “My notes” heading, despite reporting that a summary existed.
- I independently recovered the stored system audio and missing transcript tail, then saved recovered notes in the existing Page. The notes are now usable, but that manual recovery did not repair the original upload or processing state.
- A preserved 238,776,338-byte audio journal contains 1,497,016 frames with continuous per-channel sequence/sample positions. All stored Opus frames decoded successfully. The recovered system-audio duration is 4:57:25.745.
- The first manual reprocessing attempt at 07:07 UTC returned HTTP 409. Follow-up reads confirmed the recovered Page was unchanged, the server still reported recording, and local delivery remained finalizing with the HTTP 413 failure. The preserved audio journal and recovered audio file both matched their pre-retry SHA-256 hashes.
- Before the second attempt, I backed up the current revised Page as well. The second reprocessing request left those notes unchanged, and both preserved audio files still matched their earlier SHA-256 hashes.
- No application code or original recording data was edited, and no restart or cache reset was performed.

HTTP 413 is verified. A request limit is a possible cause, but the exact rejected limit and its relationship to duration are unconfirmed. The reprocessing conflict is now explained by the response below; the underlying HTTP 413 limit remains unconfirmed.

I searched for existing reports before filing and rechecked for Meetings/HTTP 413 and “Taking notes” matches. #21408 concerns long dictation failures in a different recording flow; I found no other issue describing this Meetings finalization failure.

Could you investigate why finalization is rejected and how to complete or repair this existing recording state without replacing the recovered notes?

No audio, transcript contents, meeting identifiers, private paths, credentials, or raw logs are attached.

items.title: VS Code extension: Windows setup fails when not elevated — one-time sandbox provisioning (CodexSandbox users, firewall, WFP) requires admin

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
### Environment
- Windows 11 Pro (build 22631)
- Codex VS Code extension (`openai.chatgpt`, version 26.x, bundled CLI 0.160.0)
- No third-party sandbox tooling; default user account in the local Administrators group

### Symptom
On first open of the Codex VS Code extension, onboarding is stuck at the **"Complete Windows setup"** step and reports:

- *"Windows setup not completed / configuration failed to load / continue without administrator access"*
- (Chinese UI: *"Windows 设置未完成 配置加载未成功 在没有管理员访问权限的情况下继续"*)

### Root cause
The "Windows setup" step runs the bundled `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe`, which must perform a **one-time privileged provisioning**:

1. **Create two local user accounts**: `CodexSandboxOffline` and `CodexSandboxOnline`
2. **Create Windows Firewall rules**: `codex_sandbox_offline_block_loopback_udp`, `codex_sandbox_offline_block_loopback_tcp`, `codex_sandbox_offline_block_outbound`
3. **Install WFP (Windows Filtering Platform) filters** for the offline sandbox user (12 filters)

All three require administrator privileges. When the setup helper runs unelevated (VS Code started normally, or the account is not in Administrators), user creation and firewall/WFP setup fail, so the marker/config load fails and Codex offers the *"continue without administrator access"* fallback.

### Why it works afterward without admin
The privileged part is **one-time**. After it succeeds once:

- The two sandbox users and the firewall rules persist system-wide.
- Every later launch only performs an incremental **"setup refresh"**: granting read/write ACEs to those existing sandbox users on the current user's own paths — which needs **no elevation**.

Two benign failures during refresh are tolerated and do not block usage (both access-denied, error 5): granting a read ACE on a protected packaged-app folder (WindowsApps), and hiding another user profile directory (Default profile).

### Fix (verified)
1. Verify current state (elevated PowerShell):
   ```powershell
   net user | findstr CodexSandbox
   Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "codex_sandbox*" | Select DisplayName, Enabled
   ```
   Missing accounts → the one-time elevated setup was never completed.
2. Complete the setup **once with elevation**: close VS Code, reopen it via *"Run as administrator"* and let the setup step finish — or run the bundled CLI once from an elevated terminal (`…\.vscode\extensions\openai.chatgpt-*\bin\windows-x86_64\codex.exe`).
3. If the setup marker is broken (marker file exists but users were never created, e.g. from a failed partial run), delete `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\setup_marker.json` and the `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox-secrets` folder, then repeat step 2.
4. Afterward, use VS Code normally — no permanent elevation needed.
5. If the account can never be an administrator, an administrator must perform step 2 once; the sandbox users + firewall rules then work for the standard user too.

### Notes
- Choosing *"continue without administrator access"* runs with **degraded isolation** (no user-based sandbox) and may re-prompt later — fix the setup instead.
- The Windows sandbox setup is **independent of sign-in**: sign-in goes through the configured model provider (`requires_openai_auth = false` with a proxy-managed token). Reaching this setup step means auth already passed.
- This is a distinct failure stage from #35965 (desktop app where the elevated helper never launches) and #24490 (helper fails with "The parameter is incorrect"): here the helper runs, but the one-time privileged provisioning (users + firewall + WFP) fails when unelevated.

### Related issues
- #35965 – Windows app: "Finish Windows setup" never starts elevated sandbox setup; `sandbox = "unelevated"` works
- #24490 – Windows elevated sandbox setup helper shows "The parameter is incorrect" even with clean CODEX_HOME and short ASCII npm path; unelevated works

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

The documented `browser-use` initialization fails in Codex on macOS arm64 with `No native build was found`. In the installed plugin cache, the `classic-level` macOS prebuild directory exists but is empty.

Codex search and a separate supported CUA browser entry point work in the same task. This isolates the observed failure to this plugin bootstrap path.

## Environment

- ChatGPT desktop app with Codex: `26.1007.21159`, build `20052` (read from the installed app's Info.plist).
- macOS: `27.0.1` (`26A434`), `arm64`.
- Installed skill/plugin cache: `browser-use@openai-bundled`, `0.1.0-alpha2`.
- Native dependency: `classic-level`, `3.0.0`.
- The failing Node REPL reports Node `24.21.0`, ABI `137`.
- The loading helper is `ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/cua_node/bin/node_repl`, signed by OpenAI with Team ID `2DC432GLL2` and hardened runtime enabled.

## Steps to reproduce in the affected installation

1. Start a Codex task and use the installed Browser skill.
2. Run the skill's documented initialization in Node REPL, replacing `<plugin-cache>` with the installed browser-use cache directory:

```js
const { setupAtlasRuntime } = await import("<plugin-cache>/scripts/browser-client.mjs");
await setupAtlasRuntime({ globals: globalThis });
globalThis.browser = await agent.browsers.get("iab");
```

3. Initialization fails before the browser can be selected.
4. Inspect this directory:

```text
~/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled/browser-use/0.1.0-alpha2/scripts/node_modules/classic-level/prebuilds/darwin-x64+arm64/
```

The directory is present and contains no `classic-level.node` file.

## Actual error

```text
No native build was found for platform=darwin arch=arm64 runtime=node abi=137 uv=1 armv=8 libc=glibc node=24.21.0
    loaded from: <plugin-cache>/scripts/node_modules/classic-level
```

## Controlled diagnostic attempt, subsequently rolled back

To distinguish a missing binary from an architecture/Node compatibility issue, the missing file was temporarily supplied from the upstream npm `classic-level@3.0.0` tarball. The tarball SHA512 matched the registry's published integrity value.

- The upstream file is a universal Mach-O binary containing x86_64 and arm64.
- The independent bundled workspace Node `24.19.0` could load `classic-level` with this file.
- After resetting the Node REPL session, the Codex helper rejected the same file with:

```text
code signature ... not valid for use in process:
mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs
```

`codesign -dv` on the upstream file showed `Signature=adhoc` and `TeamIdentifier=not set`, while the Codex helper has OpenAI's Team ID. This secondary signature failure occurred only during the temporary upstream-component restoration.

The added file was removed after verifying its hash against the retained upstream copy. The original plugin-cache state was restored. No app/helper binaries were re-signed, and no security settings were changed.

## Working comparison and scope

The supported CUA API successfully opened `https://matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org/` in the in-app browser and returned its populated leaderboard and controls. Direct HTTPS access to that public page also returned HTTP 200.

I have not reproduced this on a clean plugin reinstall or established why the macOS prebuild is absent. The evidence above describes the installed cache and the documented bootstrap path; it does not establish a release-wide packaging defect.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please check whether the plugin installation/reconciliation path can leave the macOS prebuild directory empty or register an older Browser skill against an incompatible current runtime. Provide a supported way to restore a complete native payload that loads under the helper's signing policy, and surface a clear component-installation/runtime error when this bootstrap fails.

## Related reports

- #37324: `classic-level.node` signature failure in the Chrome plugin, including a Team ID mismatch after local re-signing.
- #43385: Chrome native-host signature inconsistency and browser-control timeout.

The primary observed failure here is the empty macOS prebuild directory in `browser-use` `0.1.0-alpha2`; the separately documented restoration experiment may help clarify the supported recovery path.

items.body:
### Summary
In a dot-delegated Windows Codex task, an official per-command `require_escalated` request was rejected before execution by a granular approval policy. Separately, a bounded Windows Job setup diagnostic failed with error 1314. We cannot determine the effective executor/backend and supported permission path from the available diagnostics. These are separate observations; a shared root cause is NOT established.

### Version / environment
- App/bundled executor version: UNKNOWN; the delegated environment's app-version tool reports that app updates are only available on the local desktop host.
- Installed CLI version: UNKNOWN; `codex` is not on the current tool environment's PATH.
- Surface: dot -> connected Windows computer -> delegated Codex task.
- Local config declaration: `[windows]\nsandbox = "elevated"`. This does not establish the incident-time active backend.
- Current read-only OS observation: `Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200`, PowerShell Core 7.6.5. Windows edition/full patch revision are unknown. The incident did not record immutable host identity, so these are NOT asserted as incident-time versions.
- Explicit CODEX_HOME is unset; default `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` and its `.sandbox` directory exist. `.sandbox/sandbox.log` was not found.

### Observation 1: approval request rejected before execution
An attempt to run a pinned read-only preflight for existing local application files and owner metadata returned:
```text
approval policy is Granular(GranularApprovalConfig { sandbox_approval: false, rules: false, skill_approval: false, request_permissions: true, mcp_elicitations: true }); reject command — you cannot ask for escalated permissions if the approval policy is Granular(GranularApprovalConfig { sandbox_approval: false, rules: false, skill_approval: false, request_permissions: true, mcp_elicitations: true })
```
The command did not run. No separate request_permissions tool was exposed in that delegated task. Default execution had access-denied/Win32 5 errors for the required existing files/owner query. We did not change ACLs or disable the sandbox.
A later task describes workspace-write/auto_review; we do not assume that later declaration replaces the earlier incident policy.

### Observation 2: separate Windows Job setup failure
Existing diagnostic recorded on 2026-10-10 around 01:02:39–01:02:43 UTC:
- CreateJobObjectW: success.
- SetInformationJobObject: class 9, x64 extended structure size 144 bytes/alignment 8.
- LimitFlags: 0x209 (WORKINGSET | ACTIVE_PROCESS | JOB_MEMORY).
- ActiveProcessLimit: 4.
- Minimum/maximum working set: 1 MiB / 64 MiB.
- JobMemoryLimit: 256 MiB.
- Other fields zero; no breakaway flags.
- Return: 0; immediately captured GetLastError: 1314.
- AssignProcessToJobObject was NOT reached; zero child processes created.
- CloseHandle succeeded; diagnostic exited 1 after approximately 0.256 seconds.
This is evidence from a one-time closed diagnostic, not a claim of a reproducible Codex defect or proof of a specific missing privilege. No private account data, credentials, provider calls or application activation were involved. It has not been rerun.

### Expected behavior / requested guidance
